boundary.candidate_identity_rule: source-qualified/run-stable identity; never join by bare short id alone

source_lineage_warnings: The current 00:00 worker wave was largely executed under control revision 3/config revision 2; this comparator itself observes control revision 4. Evidence is judged from executed artifacts, not from pretending revision-4 explorer policy was already executed.

Terminal same-run follow-up artifacts for long_horizon, reasoning, scientist_agents and self_improvement depend on explicitly referenced same-role base checkpoints; assessments preserve those source-qualified chains.

Primary-verification STATE advanced after Run7 and contains source-specific corrections for failure_evidence/FE-021 and multi_agent/multi-agent-g1-C18; those corrections are applied only to the matching candidate identities.

Author code, same-paper reruns, simulation replays and fixed-corpus rescoring remain reproducibility support rather than independent numerical replication unless provenance-equivalent independent reruns are present.
assessments: Paper-level drift-signal/downstream evidence remains useful, but the current public release exposes frozen-feature/CKA traces rather than the surfaced CUSUM alarm/reset stage; the inspected paper text also does not surface a numeric kappa_h. The released MVP-Shift path is oracle-only, reading ground-truth change type rather than detector output. Keep the mechanism promising but do not call the released artifact an end-to-end detector-to-policy reproduction.

Peer-reviewed UAI-2025 best-arm identification gives both a formal no-worse-than-online shadow path under a valid bias bound and deliberate misleading-history experiments. Theorem 4.1 makes historical savings candidate-local and zero when bias is too large. Strong source-domain evidence; transfer to generic research evaluation/BO is a hypothesis and the valid bias bound is a critical assumption.

Narrow prior safe-transfer interpretation: a 2026 controlled MTBO audit reports negative transfer and even correlation-sign failures on affinely related tasks, so learned similarity/correlation alone is not a sufficient safety gate. Retain source suppression as a mechanism, but require a target-only shadow or explicit admissibility/bias test before claiming negative-transfer protection.

Exact stratified block e-processes support optional stopping with past-determined block sizes and show heterogeneous-strata gains in 1,000-run simulations. The guarantee is for the paper's independent completed-block/Bernoulli structure; repeated correlated trajectories within a task must be summarized or separately modeled.

Primary time-uniform paired-sample theory explicitly permits dependence inside each arriving X/Y pair and can tighten two-sample bounds. It does not permit arbitrary serial dependence across task pairs, so it is a pairing correction rather than a cluster-dependence solution.

Possibly-dependent uSPRT/nmSPRT work gives strong simulations and asymptotic guarantees after burn-in; the paper itself shows early no-burn monitoring can over-reject. Useful efficient screen only when martingale/regularity and burn-in diagnostics hold; not an exact certificate for 10–50 arbitrary task clusters.

Design-based confidence sequences provide time-uniform inference from known randomized assignment and include a concrete Netflix early-stop example. Strong when assignment is evaluator-controlled; not a generic fix for observational benchmarks, interference, or unmodeled cluster dependence.

Classical cluster-randomized group-sequential work reports satisfactory behavior for four of five statistics with 10 clusters per intervention in the tested binary CRT design. This supports a prespecified-look fallback, not arbitrary-look anytime validity, and post-stop effect estimation was not established.

Matched Terminal-Bench hardening ablations show exploit displacement: blind+pool improves unhinted attacks while judge-filtered hinted ASR rises 42.9%→50.7% (+7.8 pp, reported p<0.01). Strong within-study negative evidence that attack-class coverage matters; same study/fixed evaluation corpus, not independent or per-snapshot online re-attack.

Peer-reviewed NAACL-2025 adaptive indirect-prompt-injection study directly compares original/non-adaptive defense evaluation against defense-aware adaptive attacks across eight defenses and two agent backbones, with large ASR reversals. Strong matched robustness evidence under a white-box threat model; benign utility is not evaluated and scope is indirect prompt injection.

A 2026 preprint reports severe first-action invalid/refusal shifts and retry cascades for specific StruQ/SecAlign open-model agent setups, alongside weak attack discrimination. Quantitative failure evidence is substantial but method/model/harness-specific, potentially interface-mediated, and not independently replicated.

Primary audit verifies AgentSuite Filtering rank reversals from committed CSVs and confirms Filtering re-scores the same Original trajectories rather than rerunning agents. Scope correction: Filtering removes FIX/TODO as well as REMOVE, so evidence supports leaderboard sensitivity to task-composition/audit flags, not that every excluded task is objectively invalid; Fixed is a separate condition.

Direct SWE-bench Verified intervention study couples a 0.6B online failure monitor with FPR-budgeted restart policies: at 10% FPR RestartSmart adds roughly 3–4 pp resolution across three policies, while 5% FPR monitoring saves 14.6–20.4% tokens. Patience/cold-restart ablations isolate false-positive disruption and artifact carryover. Strong matched preprint evidence; no independent replication and domain is SWE.

Peer-reviewed rollback study shows a non-monotonic information-horizon effect on ALFWorld: Qwen2.5-14B rises from about 80.6% no-wait to 88.1% near k=6 before declining. Supports delayed diagnosis as a control variable, but does not isolate historical target-selection rules and is compute-expensive.

Peer-reviewed web-agent results show explicit model-controlled rollback improves full success over OneWay and BestFirst across Mind2Web-Live/WebVoyager and several backbones while using fewer switches than BestFirst. Trigger and target selector change together, so this is not a pure target-selector ablation; URL reset also does not establish safety for irreversible web effects.

Order-swap inconsistency is directly tested as a selective-compute trigger: GPT-4.1 selective LWE reaches 0.648/0.808 pair accuracy at 3.9× cost versus full LWE 0.646/0.727 at 10.9× on VL/MM RewardBench. Inconsistent subsets benefit strongly, but many consistent-wrong cases remain and cost can explode when the base judge is broadly unstable.

Peer-reviewed EACL-2026 prompt-optimizer poisoning experiments show iterative optimization can amplify corrupted feedback, including material ASR increases with only 10% poisoned data. Strong failure mechanism evidence, but it is adversarial poisoning rather than stochastic judge-noise calibration and many trends are single-run.

Primary audit verifies strong judge-error correlation: nine judges yield Kish n_eff≈2.18 on 1,000 MNLI items and ≈1.99 on RewardBench; panels do not reliably beat the best single judge. CoT raises correlation in the tested setup. Treat effective sample size as measured configuration-specific evidence, not a universal constant or direct open-ended-agent estimate.

Peer-reviewed five-seed AGMP study reports broad online SNN benchmarks, continual-learning comparisons and large component ablations (e.g. Split N-MNIST 82.6% full vs 51.3% without the slow astrocytic gate). Evidence supports a slow stability/metaplasticity role in the tested SNN setting; no public implementation/independent rerun was found, feedback is not fully local, and task-free/open-world claims are unsupported.

Provenance correction: the Aug-2025 paper-era Memento tree contains no parametric-memory implementation, so the Oct-2025 released row-level validation defect cannot be attributed to the paper experiments. Table 4 still supports a positive between-arm CBR gap, but the no-CBR arm rises more from iteration 1→5, so the shared upward slope is not memory-specific continual-learning evidence.

Pinned public code/tests support fail-closed evidence validation before durable stage mutation and document a real prior early-completion bypass. Current repair adds final-stage/read-side checks, but privileged early completion still rests on a caller-supplied boolean ('lock, not signature'). Strong implementation evidence for separating evidence validity from transition authority; no quantitative end-to-end efficacy result.

CovCal supplies direct finite-sample selective-risk/coverage evidence for Lean-as-Judge: high proved coverage corresponds to ~96% correctness while low coverage can collapse to ~20%; a sparse formalizer makes certificates infeasible whereas a specialized one enables ~48% acceptance at ~0.98 accuracy. Strong judging evidence, but proof-search routing transfer is not directly tested.

The v3 Lean cost-quality router reports 28.9% cost reduction at parity accuracy and 7.9% accuracy gain at parity cost using logistic success probabilities, but no Brier/ECE/reliability/selective-risk diagnostics are reported. Preserve the efficiency result inside its 42/43-problem split; probability calibration and distribution-shift robustness remain unverified.

Snapshotting evidence shows execution substrate can dominate cost: repeated Lean reconstruction is reported >99% of branch wall time in the tested setting, with 5.6–50× speedups (average 14×) from live-state snapshots. This strongly narrows portability of token/SFLOP-only router costs, but no surfaced experiment combines snapshotting with the learned router.

Neighboring adaptive-retrieval systems report +5.6 pp and +10.1 F1 with fewer retrieval calls, supporting selective mid-course retrieval in QA. This is transfer evidence only and should not be scored as a demonstrated Lean theorem-proving gain.

A 423-spec Lean vericoding study reports 95% solve rate at K=50 and a difficulty-dependent search-structure result: context branching helps intermediate cases/lower token cost while uninterrupted iteration remains better on the hardest tasks. Exact per-difficulty tables and public code were not recovered, limiting reproducibility and precise causal grading.

AutoResearchEval provides unusually broad process-diagnostic evidence (800 trajectories, 73k tool calls, 12,712 failure attributions) and strong expert/judge agreement; 'uncorrected self-awareness' appears in 82.5% of analyses. This supports the prevalence of the failure, not the proposed mandatory closure controller, because no intervention ablation is tested.

Faraday's direct continuation ablation reports reward collapse and policy-divergence/entropy instability after removing turn-level credit assignment, while the matched credit-retaining continuation improves. Strong within-system training-stability evidence, but credit labels come from the same learned rubric-judge stack and broad scientific-outcome causality is not isolated.

Matched Faraday ablations support a researcher–coder hierarchy: removing the coding-agent tool under the same base/training setup underperforms before eventual collapse, and swapping to a stronger coder improves held-out replication scores without retraining the researcher. Treat the external coder as part of total capability/compute; evidence is Replica paper-replication, not open-ended discovery.

Scope correction: rubric-judge vs human Kendall tau is only 0.19 (baseline judge 0.15), and disputed-pair human preference for the rubric judge is 63% with p=0.109. The judge appears lower-noise internally but is not independently validated as a scientific oracle; held-out Faraday advantages remain rubric-judge results with this caveat.

PACE's same-loop comparison is stronger than previously summarized: greedy, fixed-n paired, online-FDR and anytime-valid PACE are directly compared, with greedy producing many false/harmful commits while paired/PACE preserve genuine gains. However PACE remains a per-decision optional-stopping result, not an unbounded lineage-familywise theorem, and no public raw paired traces/code were found for exact replay.

Matched WebArena release-engineering ablation cuts pass→fail rate from 14.8% without the flip gate to 3.1% with it and bad releases from 4 to 0, while the no-gate arm is 0.8 pp higher on one final test. Strong evidence for downside/regression control, not endpoint-accuracy maximization or adaptive-holdout validity.

Fixed task sets/total exposure reveal a sharply non-monotonic update schedule: batch 20 improves ID +9.1 pp while batch 10 and 80 regress −14.5 and −16.4 pp. This is strong evidence that update packaging/cadence is a separate failure axis from acceptance statistics; protocol-specific optimum should not be universalized.

Five-round Terminal-Bench evolution shows pre-commit VaG reaching 72% vs ungated 50%, with behavioral-replay and joint-gain ablations costing 10 and 8 pp respectively; post-hoc source deletion recovers little of inherited contamination. Strong matched preprint evidence for persistent-skill admission controls, but Holdout-14 is repeatedly reused without sequential correction and lockbox transfer samples are small.

ICML-2026 workshop simulation directly compares reusable holdout, anytime-FDR, e-process spending and a three-gate statistical/capacity/domain contract on the same synthetic proposal distribution; the full contract reports much lower harmful-adoption and rollback/cost metrics. Useful compositional mechanism evidence only: synthetic streams, no real evolving LLM agent, no independent code rerun found.

Public SGM code/raw outputs make within-SGM policy replay plausible and expose an explicit proposal ledger/screen-confirm spending path, but README commands reference absent current-tree paths. This is a reproducibility/provenance defect, not evidence against the paper; cross-PACE identical-stream replay remains blocked by missing PACE raw outcomes.

scope_corrections.correction: Do not treat raw CKA CSVs or the oracle MVP-Shift path as a released end-to-end CUSUM detector/diagnosis/policy implementation. FAR, Episode Recall and normalized detection time remain missing from surfaced evaluation.
Apparent task relatedness or learned correlation is not itself a negative-transfer guarantee; current evidence requires a target-only shadow or explicit source-admissibility/bias check.
Primary audit verifies rank sensitivity under Filtering but not universal invalidity of all excluded tasks; Filtering re-scores existing trajectories and differs from the separate Fixed condition.
n_eff≈2 is measured for the audited judge panels/datasets, not a universal effective judge count; panel accuracy can be below the best single judge.

The later released row-level split is not provenance-equivalent to the paper-era experiment. Paper Table 4 supports a between-arm CBR effect, not memory-specific attribution of the shared iteration slope.
Evidence validity and transition authority are orthogonal; the current early-completion standing is still represented by a caller-supplied flag rather than an unforgeable capability.
The router's efficiency result is a decision-performance result, not evidence that q_hat is calibrated as a probability under distribution shift.
High prevalence of uncorrected self-awareness diagnoses a failure class but does not causally validate the proposed artifact-grounded closure intervention.
Human alignment is modest and disputed-pair preference is not statistically significant; rubric-judge task gains remain judge-scored evidence rather than independent scientific truth.
PACE controls per-decision optional stopping; lineage/global familywise control remains a separate unresolved dimension, and exact published-stream replay is blocked by missing public raw traces.
Strong content-admission/lineage-contamination evidence does not imply the repeatedly reused Holdout-14 gate is statistically calibrated for long adaptive evolution.
The multi-layer comparison is synthetic simulation evidence and must not be merged with real-agent VaG/SEAGym/PACE evidence as if all came from one deployment experiment.
